symbols.doc: A building's plan, which its walls, roof, openings and dressing all build against, so they agree by construction. Local meters: the origin is the center of the whole footprint at ground level, and the door faces +z.
symbols.name: BuildingPlan

symbols.doc: The palette families native to a region. Empty means every family.
symbols.name: NativeFamilies

symbols.doc: A procedural operator. Code, written by Claude or a person, versioned in its ID. `build` must be pure: the same params, seed and input give the same output.
symbols.name: Primitive

symbols.doc: A primitive with its parameter types erased, so primitives of different shapes share one list. Gaia checks stored values against `params` before it calls `build`, which is why the erased signature can accept anything.

files.doc: Seeded randomness with named sub-streams. A primitive forks a stream per concern, so drawing more values in one place never shifts another.

symbols.name: seedOf

files.doc: What a Relief primitive produces: a region's ground shape as plain data. A height field is a small expression tree that one evaluator samples, so a landform crosses worker boundaries and hashes like any other output. Coordinates are meters in the region's own frame: origin at its center, +x east, +z south. Heights are meters above the region's base.

symbols.doc: A stream bed from source to mouth. The world solves its waterline so the water always sits in the ground.
symbols.name: StreamBed

symbols.doc: A hollow that holds still water; the world fills it to just below its lowest rim point.
symbols.name: PondBed

files.doc: The relief budget: how much the land may rise and fall. Low relief keeps sight lines short, so nothing far away ever needs drawing in detail.

symbols.doc: Measures relief over the samples where `include` is true (all when omitted).
symbols.name: measureRelief

symbols.doc: True when the report fits the budget, keeping `rangeMargin` meters spare for water to cut into.
symbols.name: withinBudget

files.doc: How water moves: a stream runs down its solved waterline, faster where its channel narrows or its line falls, and a pond lies still. The renderer scrolls the surface along this flow and lets wading rings drift with it.

symbols.doc: A velocity on the ground plane, meters per second.
symbols.name: Velocity

symbols.doc: The velocity at each station, as x, z pairs: along the stream toward its lower end, where the same water through a narrower channel runs faster.
symbols.name: streamFlow

symbols.doc: The water's velocity at a point: the nearest stream's flow where its surface reaches, still elsewhere.
symbols.name: flowAt

files.doc: Where a landmark stands. A landmark is meant to be seen from far away, so its site is the most prominent gentle, dry ground of its region: a knoll or a rise near the region's heart, clear of water and of what already stands. Its footprint is then leveled into the baked lattice, blending back into the land, as a cottage's pad is.

symbols.doc: The most prominent gentle, dry spot in a region for a landmark of footprint `radius`, keeping clear of `avoid`; null when the region has no room.
symbols.name: findLandmarkSite

symbols.doc: Levels a disc of ground to its mean height, blending back to the land; returns that height.
symbols.name: levelDisc

files.doc: The world's one height truth: a square lattice of baked heights. The renderer's mesh, the grass, the trees and every measurement read these same samples with the same triangle interpolation, so they cannot disagree.

symbols.doc: Height at any point, interpolated exactly as the mesh draws it: each cell splits along the diagonal from (ix+1, iz) to (ix, iz+1).
symbols.name: heightAt

symbols.doc: Slope in degrees at a point, from the cell's gradient.
symbols.name: slopeAt

files.doc: A stand-in for the world layout: where each region's center sits and its ground level. The real layout comes from the directory tree.

symbols.name: layoutSites

files.doc: Trails between a world's places. A trail's look is a `RouteSpec` Jev fills; its route is never chosen, it is found over the baked ground: the cheapest way at a gentle grade, around steep ground and deep water, across a stream where it is narrow, wandering as freely as the spec's winding says. The composition budget then keeps the most wanted trails that fit, so trails never dominate a region. Ever…

symbols.doc: One end of a trail: a place, such as a cottage's door or a landmark's foot.
symbols.name: TrailEnd

symbols.doc: A trail Jev wants: two places, how it looks, and how much Jev wants it.

symbols.doc: The cheapest chain of cells between two points, or null when none exists.

symbols.doc: Chaikin corner cutting, then resampling every `spacing` meters: a trail curves instead of turning on a grid.

symbols.doc: Each region's walkable ground, square meters.

symbols.doc: Routes the trails Jev wants, most wanted first, and keeps each only while every region it crosses stays within the composition budget: at most `TRAILS.routesPerRegion` trails, covering at most `TRAILS.share` of its ground. symbols.name: nearSegments

symbols.doc: Eases the baked ground under each trail toward the tread's own smoothed grade, blending back to the land over `TRAILS.blend` meters, as a cottage's pad does. symbols.name: levelTrails

symbols.doc: Signed distance from each lattice sample to the nearest trail's edge, meters: negative on the tread, capped at `TRAILS.reach`. The ground paints worn earth from it and the grass parts along it; water reads as far.

symbols.doc: A trail's place packed in one number: its index, plus how far along it (0 to 1) in the fraction.

files.doc: Where the understory stands: rocks in groups, bushes in thickets, flowers in drifts. Every placement is grounded so nothing floats: a solid thing sits below the lowest ground under its footpr…

symbols.name: scatterComponents

files.doc: How far a person standing on the ground can see the ground. A ray marches outward along each bearing; a sample is visible when it rises above every nearer sample's line of sight. The farthest visible sample per bearing is where that direction's view of the land ends.

Where a building stands and how it meets the ground. A site is chosen on dry, gentle ground near water, facing its door toward it; then a pad is leveled into the baked lattice under the house and its yard, blending back into the land over a few meters, so the walls, the walk and the grass all stand on the same flat ground and nothing floats.

symbols.doc: A capsule of ground from (ax, az) to (bx, bz), in world meters.
symbols.name: Capsule

symbols.doc: A circle of ground, such as the lot a building or a landmark is laid out on.
symbols.name: Circle

symbols.doc: Meters over which a pad blends back into the land.
symbols.name: PAD_BLEND

symbols.doc: A rectangle in the building's own frame, such as the reach of a mill wheel or a tower beside the house.
symbols.name: Extent

symbols.doc: The yard in the building's own frame: the house, a margin around it, the walk out front, and anything beside it.
symbols.name: yardOf

symbols.doc: A point in the building's frame, in the world, as Three's rotation about y places it.
symbols.name: siteToWorld

symbols.doc: True when (x, z) is within `margin` of the building's walls.
symbols.name: insideFootprint

symbols.doc: The yard's samples, every `step` meters, in the world.
symbols.name: yardSamples

symbols.doc: The gentlest dry spot near the middle reach of a stream, its door facing the water; without streams, the gentlest dry spot inside the world. A site keeps `apart` meters from every site already `taken`, and its yard covers `beside` too.
symbols.name: findSite

symbols.doc: Levels the lattice under the yard to the site's level, blending back to the land over PAD_BLEND meters.
symbols.name: levelPad

symbols.doc: Ground kept clear of grass: the house's floor and the walk out from its door.
symbols.name: clearingsOf

files.doc: What a person cannot walk through: tree trunks, rocks, bushes and a house's walls. Each solid is the convex hull of its outline on the ground, rounded by a radius (a trunk is one point rounded by the trunk's own radius), so its edge has a direction everywhere and a walker slides around it without catching. Built once from placements; every step of a walk asks how far the nearest edge is.

symbols.doc: One thing in the way, as its outline on the ground in world meters.
symbols.name: SolidShape

symbols.doc: The solids of one world, indexed by ground cells so a step only asks about the few nearby.
symbols.name: Solids

symbols.doc: Andrew's monotone chain: the convex hull of x, z pairs, counter-clockwise, without collinear corners.
symbols.name: hullOf

symbols.doc: Indexes solids from their outlines on the ground.
symbols.name: solidsOf

symbols.doc: A placed component's outline on the ground: its reach in `outline.length` directions at scale 1, turned and scaled as Three places it, times `share`.
symbols.name: outlineShape

symbols.doc: A building's walls: each of its masses' footprints on its site.
symbols.name: wallsShape

symbols.doc: A walker's body, from just above the ground to the top of its head, meters above a thing's base.
symbols.name: BODY_BAND

symbols.doc: The solids of a built thing standing at (x, y, z), turned by `yaw` as Three turns it: each solid piece's outline across a walker's body height. A piece wholly above or below that band stops nothing, so a walker passes under a lintel and through a doorway between two stones. Nor does a piece that only grows in as the thing declines, such as fallen stone.
symbols.name: piecesShapes

symbols.doc: The nearest edge to a point: signed distance (negative inside) and the outward direction there.
symbols.name: Edge

symbols.doc: The nearest solid's edge to (x, z), written into `out`; `out.distance` is `REACH` when nothing is that close. Accurate within `REACH` meters.
symbols.name: nearestEdge

symbols.doc: How far (x, z) is from the nearest solid's edge, negative inside one; at most 2 m.
symbols.name: clearanceAt

files.doc: Walking at eye height, one pure step at a time. Solid things stop a person and turn the step aside along their edge; water never does. A person wades more slowly as the water deepens and swims where it is deep, eyes a little above the surface. A walk to a tapped point plans its way around whatever stands between, follows that way smoothly, and ends on arrival. Nothing bounds a walk: past the codeb…

symbols.doc: How far a person's body keeps from the edge of anything solid, meters.
symbols.name: BODY_RADIUS

symbols.doc: Where the person wants to go: a direction on the ground (length up to 1) and a speed in meters per second.
symbols.name: Intent

symbols.doc: Water depth per lattice sample, 0 where there is no water: interpolates like the ground does.
symbols.name: depthField

symbols.doc: Water depth at a point: the water surface minus the ground, never below 0, and none in the wild.
symbols.name: waterDepthAt

symbols.doc: The share of full speed left at `depth`: wading slows to 40% by 1.1 m, and swimming is slower again.
symbols.name: wadeSpeed

symbols.doc: How a person stands at a point: their eyes' height, the water's depth, and how far they swim, 0 to 1.
symbols.name: Stance

symbols.doc: Eyes stay 1.6 m above the ground until the water nears them; then, as the bottom falls away, they ease down to `SWIM.eye` above the surface. The height is smooth in depth, so it never jumps, and never below the surface.
symbols.name: stanceAt

symbols.doc: Moves by (mx, mz), turning aside along the edge of any solid in the way: each part of the step that would end inside one is pushed back out along the edge's normal, which keeps only the part running along it. A part that cannot be freed (a wedge between two solids) is not taken.
symbols.name: moveBy

symbols.doc: One step of walking. Speed falls as the water deepens and is slowest swimming; water never stops the step. Solids turn it aside along their edge, so pushing straight at one stops and pushing at an angle slides.
symbols.name: walkStep

symbols.doc: A walk to a tapped point.
symbols.name: Walk

symbols.doc: One step of a walk to a target, and whether the walk goes on.
symbols.name: Approach

symbols.doc: Whether a body walking straight from a to b stays `room` meters clear of every solid.
symbols.name: clearWay

symbols.doc: The way from `from` to `to` around everything solid: straight when nothing is in the way, otherwise the shortest way on a grid laid along the walk, pulled taut to its corners. A tap on a solid walks up to the face that was tapped; when nothing reaches the target (solids ring it), the way ends at the nearest place that can be reached.
symbols.name: planWalk

symbols.doc: A* on a grid laid along the walk, where cells nearer a solid than the body and its clearance are closed, pulled taut.
symbols.name: routeAround

symbols.doc: The point `ahead` meters along the way past the walker's place on it; moves on to the next leg once the walker passes a leg's end.
symbols.name: pursue

symbols.doc: One step of a walk along its planned way, through the same movement as a held key, so wading, swimming and solids work as they do for any walk. The walker heads for a point a little ahead along the way, so it rounds each corner in a curve, and jogs while the target is far.

files.doc: Water is solved from the ground, never placed on it. A stream's waterline is a running minimum of the ground along its bed, so it only descends and always sits below the land it runs through; the channel is then cut below that line. A pond fills to just under the lowest point of its rim. The carve math follows v2's linear carve (src/world/compile/linear/carve.ts).

symbols.doc: How far the banks reach beyond the water's edge, meters.

symbols.doc: Solves a stream's waterline over `path` (world x, z pairs, source first).

symbols.doc: Cuts the channel and its banks into `heights`, and records the water level where the banks contain it.
symbols.name: carveStream

symbols.doc: Fills a pond to just under its rim, then cuts a gentle bed below the level. Null when the hollow cannot hold water.
symbols.name: solvePond

symbols.doc: The shore field stops counting this far from the water, meters.
symbols.name: SHORE_CAP

symbols.name: shoreField

files.doc: The wild land past the codebase's land. symbols.doc: The integer hash both sides share: a lattice corner and an octave to a number in [0, 1).

symbols.doc: Tags read from the facts in a request's state: what the stand-in matches against each option's `suits`.
symbols.name: tagsOf

symbols.doc: The deterministic stand-in judge: answers the requests `planWorldRequests` makes, exactly as Jev would receive them, without the network. Each option scores one point per fact tag its look `suits`, plus a tie-break seeded by the question and the option, so equal options spread across the world. A trail's probability grows with how many entities lean on its far end.
symbols.name: standInJev

symbols.doc: Packs discs around the origin in order: each takes the nearest free spot on rings growing outward, keeping `gap` from the others; the first sits at the origin. Each ring's angles start at a rotation seeded by `seed`.
symbols.name: pack

symbols.doc: The middle of a near-smallest circle enclosing every disc (Bădoiu and Clarkson's iteration).
symbols.name: enclosing

symbols.doc: Lays out the world from the code and Jev's judgments.
symbols.name: layoutWorld

files.doc: How much Jev sees. Every request starts with the code facts. Confidence decides whether to read more, and Jev decides what to read: each request also asks, one yes-or-no per reading, which readings would help. Unrelated state lowers Jev's accuracy, so nothing is added without a reason.

symbols.doc: One piece of extra context Gaia can add to the state.
symbols.name: Reading

symbols.doc: Confidence for choices and scores; distance from an even split for a noul, which has none.
symbols.name: certainty

files.doc: Turns a kind into Jev questions and Jev answers into a blueprint. One request per nesting level: structure first, then the details of whatever the structure chose, so the details can agree with it.

symbols.doc: Who the blueprint is for and what Jev may know while deciding.
symbols.name: Target

symbols.doc: Which primitive fills each slot, after the structure request. Absent optional slots are left out.
symbols.name: Structure

symbols.doc: Jev leans toward the first option of a choice. Shuffling in an order seeded by the target spreads that lean evenly across the world.
symbols.name: shuffled

symbols.doc: A choice or set limited to the allowed keys; an empty or missing list leaves it whole.
symbols.name: narrowed

symbols.doc: Every problem with a blueprint, so a bad answer never reaches the document.
symbols.name: validate

symbols.doc: The most probable level of a score, as Jev's docs advise, never the weighted mean.
symbols.name: topLevel

symbols.doc: The option for a file that no component stands for; it enriches the region's ground instead.
symbols.name: GROUND

symbols.doc: Jev decides which kind stands for a file, so the mapping from code to world is a judgment, not a rule table. Kinds describe themselves in `represents`.
symbols.name: planRepresentation

files.doc: The type space a kind and a library declare: its size, defaults, and a uniform sample. Everything here is read off the field declarations.

symbols.doc: How many distinct blueprints the kind admits with this library. A slot can be present only if its `on` slot is.
symbols.name: blueprintCount

symbols.doc: A sensible starting value: the middle of a scale, the first choice.
symbols.name: defaultParams

symbols.doc: Samples every field uniformly: presence, primitive, and each parameter.
symbols.name: randomSlots

files.doc: Vitality from named signals. Each signal gives a penalty from 0 to 1 and its weight sets how much that penalty can cost; penalties multiply.

symbols.doc: A named judgment Jev scores, cached by the file's content hash like any other answer.
symbols.name: JevSignal

symbols.doc: Activity is separate: recent change drives life and light, never decline.
symbols.name: activityOf

symbols.doc: A signal about a whole entity, read from the facts summed over its files.
symbols.name: EntitySignal

symbols.doc: An entity's signals: the file signals, read as shares of the whole, so a large package with one failing test declines a little and one with half its tests failing declines a lot.
symbols.name: ENTITY_SIGNALS

symbols.doc: An entity's vitality: its signals' penalties multiplied, with any named Jev judgments.
symbols.name: entityVitalityOf

symbols.doc: A small repository, its code scaled by `grow`.
symbols.name: model

symbols.doc: A fake Jev: sure about the form from facts alone, sure about the crown only once it has seen the importers, and it says the importers would help.
symbols.name: fake

symbols.doc: Facts for this mock's subject file, shaped as the Rust engine would send them.
symbols.name: SCANNER

symbols.doc: A stand-in for Jev that answers every question deterministically, with a probability spread shaped like a real response. Tests never call the network.
symbols.name: fakeJev

files.doc: Bundles the lab (the app's renderer) into ONE self-contained HTML file for pair pages: inline JS and CSS, no network requests. Outside the app there is no engine, so its status bar reads "No engine (standalone)". Usage: pnpm lab:html [out.html]

The lab (the app's renderer) as ONE self-contained HTML page: esbuild bundles app/renderer/main.ts, and the app's own index.html carries the JS and CSS inline. `pnpm lab:html` writes the page to a file; `pnpm lab:serve` rebuilds it on every change and serves it.

symbols.doc: The app's own page, with the module script swapped for the inline bundle. It reads index.html on every call, so a served page picks up edits to it.
symbols.name: labPage

files.doc: Serves the lab to a phone over Tailscale: the same one-page bundle as `pnpm lab:html`, rebuilt whenever the renderer's source changes. It listens on this machine's Tailscale address only, never on every interface, so the LAN and localhost cannot reach it. Reload the page to see a change. The page it serves posts a smoothness report every ten seconds to /telemetry, which appends each to .lab/teleme…
Prints the Jev request the planner builds for one file, exactly as it would go to OpenRouter. Nothing is sent. Usage: pnpm print-request [structure|details]

Prints, and never sends, every Jev request that judging Gaia's own world would make: the exact bodies the engine's connector would post to OpenRouter, then how many there are and what they would cost. The cost comes from the engine's own `jev.estimate`, the same code that would send them, which reads neither the key nor the network. Usage: pnpm print-world-requests [requests.json]

Writes the engine's code model of a project to a JSON snapshot, through the same `project.open` the app calls. The terrain lab's "This codebase" world reads the committed snapshot of Gaia itself. Builds the engine first. Usage: pnpm snapshot [root] [out.json]
Finds this machine's Tailscale address, so a server can listen there and nowhere else.

symbols.doc: The first IPv4 address in 100.64.0.0/10, the range Tailscale assigns its nodes from, or null when the machine has none.
symbols.name: tailscaleAddress

files.doc: Smoothness reports from the devices `pnpm lab:serve` serves: each POST to /telemetry is one small JSON object, appended as one line to a git-ignored file, so how the lab felt on a phone can be read back afterwards.

symbols.doc: The largest report accepted, bytes. A report is a few hundred.
symbols.name: TELEMETRY_LIMIT

symbols.doc: One report as a line of JSON stamped with when it arrived, or null when the body is not one JSON object.
symbols.name: telemetryLine

symbols.doc: Answers POST /telemetry: appends the report to `file`, refusing anything too large or not a JSON object.
symbols.name: handleTelemetry
